scope: Substantive refresh of an existing post at its URL, adding sources

observations.summary: Inspect at least every three years; mechanical systems generally once a year; tanks typically pumped every three to five years depending on household size, wastewater, solids and tank size; provider inspects for leaks and scum and sludge layers; do not park or drive on drainfield, do not build on or pave it, plant grasses rather than trees or shrubs.
observations.inference_limit: Federal homeowner guidance; page does not address additives or effluent filters.

observations.summary: SCCC 7.38.140(D) riser from each manhole cover to the surface to facilitate inspection and maintenance; 7.38.140(G) solids over 3/16 inch kept from the dispersal system, which an approved effluent filter may satisfy; 7.38.150(A)(5) softener and drinking water filter discharge shall not be discharged to the septic system.
observations.inference_limit: County ordinance text for new and repaired systems; existing systems may predate these requirements.

observations.summary: Oregon State University Extension, citing EPA SepticSmart: additives are unnecessary and can harm the system and environment; biological additives can disrupt treatment; chemical additives can contaminate groundwater; many products lack independent research.
observations.inference_limit: University extension article adapted from EPA materials.

observations.summary: Removed advice to add bacteria additives, an unsourced pump every 1 to 3 years schedule, an unsourced jet septic lines every 5 years schedule, a statement implying Wade s cleans tanks (the business does not pump), expert and money saving claims, a city list, a templated FAQ answer, off-topic tags and two unrelated drain images; corrected the hero alt text to the treatment tank photo; refocused the post on parts that wear out, habits and myths, linking the sourced septic maintenance guide to avoid duplicating it. Original date kept, updated set to 2026-10-30.
